title: Telemetry-gated progressive delivery CLI and orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a telemetry-gated progressive delivery CLI and orchestration layer for LTS/versioned rollouts. The feature will let release engineers and platform automation perform canaries, automated percentage ramps, feature-flag driven routing, and automatic rollback based on live telemetry (errors, latency, model-quality regressions). Goal: make safe, repeatable rollouts for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and provide an API/CLI for programmatic releases and emergency aborts.
acceptance_criteria: CLI subcommand `redwood rollout start` supports defining: cohort sizes, ramp schedule, health gates, fallback model variants, and feature-flag toggles
Orchestrator evaluates telemetry every 30s against configured gates (error-rate P50/P95 latency, model-quality delta) and advances/halts ramps accordingly
Auto-rollback triggers when gate violation persists for 2 consecutive evaluation windows or when error-rate increases > 2x baseline
Integration tests covering: successful 0->100% ramp, mid-ramp halt/rollback, and feature-flag-only toggles
UI/Console shows live waveform of metrics with annotated rollout steps and decision history
Runbook and on-call playbook added and tested in a simulated failure run

review_feedback: PM (R. Alvarez): Ensure rollout manifest supports multi-model fallback chains and explicit LTS-mapping
Observability (S. Patel): Add model-quality signal ingestion path; recommend an eventpipe for labeled evals
Security (A. Okoye): Validate CLI auth uses token-scoped checks and respects RBAC for private deployments
SRE (N. Gomez): Recommend adding circuit-breaker that forces immediate 100% fallback if control-plane latency spikes
rollout_plan: Step 0 (canary): 0.5% traffic to target variant for 15 minutes — gate checks every 30s
Step 1: 5% traffic for 30 minutes — require gates pass for at least 4 windows before advancing
Step 2: 25% traffic for 60 minutes — require stable error delta < 0.2% and p95 within +20ms of baseline
Step 3: 60% traffic for 90 minutes — verify model-quality drift < 0.5% on golden prompts
Step 4: 100% traffic — post-rollout 2h bake with lowered alert thresholds and automated canary retention
On-gate-fail: rollback to last-known-good variant, annotate event, and create auto-ticket with telemetry snapshot
risks: False positives from noisy metrics causing unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated by consecutive-window requirement and minimum sample size
Model-quality signal lag for private deployments where evals are offline — plan: use synthetic golden set and optional customer-provided eval hooks
Rollout CLI misuse by non-privileged users — mitigation: RBAC + two-person approval for non-trivial canary sizes (>5%)
State desync between console and CLI during network partitions — mitigation: idempotent operations with server-side authoritative state
runbook: How to abort: `redwood rollout abort <id>` — immediate rollback and disable further auto-advances
How to pause and inspect: `redwood rollout pause <id>` then `redwood rollout inspect <id>` to fetch annotated traces
Emergency rollback criteria: any 5xx spike > 3x baseline sustained for 2 windows triggers immediate rollback
Post-rollback actions: gather metrics snapshot, open follow-up ENG ticket, and run canary simulation in staging
